# Worksheet: Wrangling Your Data

[📥 Download the data (.csv)](data/pine_data.csv){.btn .btn-primary download="pine_data.csv"} [📥 Download the data (.xlsx)](data/pine_data.xlsx){.btn .btn-primary download="pine_data.xlsx"} [📥 Download the messy file](data/pine_needles_error.csv){.btn .btn-secondary download="pine_needles_error.csv"}

> ## How to use this worksheet
>
> Work through each part in order, at your own pace. Type every line of code yourself into a **plain R script** — do not copy-paste. Blocks marked **▶ Run this** are code you should type and execute. Blocks marked **✏️ Your turn** ask you to write, modify, or answer something. Boxes marked **🚀 If you finish early** are optional bonus material.
>
> **Every grey `r` box below is code you type into an R script — not into the Console.** Before you start: **File → New File → R Script**, and save it as `02_wrangling_data.R` in your project's `scripts/` folder. Then work down the worksheet, adding each block to the bottom of that one script, in order.
>
> **Type the `# ── Part …` header comment at the top of each block, too.** Those comment lines are not decoration — they are how your script stays navigable, how you find your way back to a block that broke, and how I find your work when I read your script. A block with no header comment is a block I cannot place. In RStudio they also show up in the document outline (the `≡` button at the bottom-left of the editor) so you can jump straight to any part.

::: callout-important
## Column names in `pine_data.csv` / `pine_data.xlsx`

Both files hold the **same six columns, with exactly these names**. Type them
exactly as written — R is case-sensitive, and `Needle_Length` or `needle_length`
will not work:

| Column             | What it is                                     |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| `source_file`      | the raw team file the row came from             |
| `team`             | field team — one team = **one tree**            |
| `replicate`        | needle number within a tree side (1-8)          |
| `side`             | sun exposure — `"shady"` or `"sunny"`           |
| `needle_length_mm` | needle length, millimetres                      |
| `needle_width_mm`  | needle width, millimetres                       |

After you read the file in, run `names(pine_df)` and check the names on your
screen against this table before you write any other code.
:::

# Part 2b · `filter()` — OR, `%in%`, and missing values

**▶ Run this:**

``` r
# ── Part 2b.1 · `filter()` ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# OR: shady side, OR any exceptionally long needle
pine_csv_df |> filter(side == "shady" | needle_length_mm > 18)

# %in%: match one of several named teams
pine_csv_df |> filter(team %in% c("botany", "waterbugs"))
```

# Part 4b · `case_when()` — recoding and binning

**▶ Run this:**

``` r
# ── Part 4b.1 · `case_when()` ───────────────────────────────────────────
pine_csv_df |>
  mutate(
    size_class = case_when(
      needle_length_mm < 13 ~ "short",
      needle_length_mm < 16 ~ "medium",
      TRUE                  ~ "long"
    )
  ) |>
  count(size_class)
```

# Part 6 · The full pipeline

**▶ Run this:**

``` r
# ── Part 6.1 · The full pipeline ────────────────────────────────────────
pine_wrangled_df <- pine_csv_df |>
  filter(needle_length_mm > 0) |>
  select(team, side, needle_length_mm, needle_width_mm) |>
  mutate(
    needle_length_cm  = needle_length_mm / 10,
    log_length = log(needle_length_mm),
    size_class = case_when(
      needle_length_mm < 13 ~ "short",
      needle_length_mm < 16 ~ "medium",
      TRUE                  ~ "long"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(side, desc(needle_length_mm))

head(pine_wrangled_df)
```

# Part 7 · Finding duplicate rows

**▶ Run this:**

``` r
# ── Part 7.1 · Finding duplicate rows ───────────────────────────────────
needle_check_df <- read_csv("data/pine_needles_error.csv")

nrow(needle_check_df)
n_distinct(needle_check_df)
```

✏️ **Your turn:** Do `nrow()` and `n_distinct()` match? \

\
`_______________________________________________________________________`

**▶ Run this:**

``` r
# ── Part 7.2 · Finding duplicate rows ───────────────────────────────────
needle_check_df |> filter(duplicated(needle_check_df))

needle_clean_df <- needle_check_df |> distinct()

nrow(needle_clean_df)
```

> ⚠️ **Watch out!** `distinct()` only catches *exact* duplicate rows — a mistiped name won't be caught. Always look at your data too.

# Part 8 · Saving your work with `write_csv()`

Everything runs one way: **`data/` (raw, read-only) → `scripts/` (your code) → `output/` (results).**

Before you save, trim to the columns worth keeping:

**▶ Run this:**

``` r
# ── Part 8.1 · Saving your work with `write_csv()` ──────────────────────
pine_out_df <- pine_wrangled_df |>
  select(team, side, needle_length_mm, needle_width_mm)

write_csv(pine_out_df, "output/pine_data_wrangled.csv")
```

Check your `output/` folder — the new CSV should be there, and `data/pine_data.csv` should be exactly as it was.

> ⚠️ **Watch out!** `write_csv()` overwrites without asking. That is fine in `output/`, because your script can rebuild anything in there. It would be a disaster in `data/`.

# Getting unstuck

When code breaks — and it will, that is normal:

1.  **Read the error message out loud.** R usually names the line and the problem.
2.  **Check the usual suspects:** did you run `library(tidyverse)` and `library(readxl)`?
    - Spelling?
    - A missing `)` or a `|>` at the *start* of a line?
3.  `?function_name` opens the built-in help page.
4.  **Bring the exact error** (copy-paste it) to class or office hours.

> 💡 **Key idea:** Every working scientist googles error messages daily. Getting stuck is not failing — it is the job.
